events.title: Henry IV at Canossa
events.shortBlurb: The excommunicated king Henry IV stood three days as a penitent in the snow before Pope Gregory VII to beg absolution…
body: In January 1077 Henry IV of Germany, excommunicated and seeing his supporters fall away, crossed the Alps by the Mont Cenis pass in one of the severest winters on record, with his wife Bertha and their infant son. Gregory VII, traveling north to judge the quarrel, had taken shelter in the Apennine castle of Canossa, held by his ally Matilda, countess of Tuscany.

There, from 25 to 27 January, the king stood before the castle gate as a penitent, barefoot amid ice and snow, fasting and begging admission. On 28 January, moved by the pleading of Matilda and of Abbot Hugh of Cluny, the king's own godfather, Gregory received Henry and loosed him from the ban.

The scene became the lasting emblem of a king humbled before the spiritual power, yet it settled little: within weeks the German princes raised Rudolf of Swabia as a rival king, and the struggle over investiture dragged on until the Concordat of Worms in 1122.
